statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-32177 is a heap-based buffer overflow in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) that allows local elevation of privilege. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (win-arm64, win-x64, win-x86) as the only affected .NET 10 package, fixed in 10.0.8 (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/399, https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/issues/11632, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.8/10.0.8.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. None of them contains the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App runtime or any WPF or Windows Forms implementation assembly (PresentationCore, PresentationFramework, System.Xaml, System.Windows.Forms and the like), and none contains a native Windows PE file. WindowsDesktop names appear only in SDK build support: Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WindowsDesktop, which holds MSBuild targets and the PresentationBuildTasks build-task assembly; Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Ref and Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Internal nupkg files that hold only package metadata; a Microsoft.Private.Winforms nupkg that holds only MSBuild props and targets besides its package metadata; a Microsoft.Internal.Runtime.WindowsDesktop.Transport nupkg that holds runtime libraries such as System.Diagnostics.EventLog and System.Security.Cryptography.Xml; and IntelliSense XML documentation files in a Microsoft.Private.Intellisense nupkg.

CVE-2026-32177 is a heap-based buffer overflow in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) that allows local elevation of privilege. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (win-x64, win-arm64) as the only affected .NET 9 package, fixed in 9.0.16 (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/399, https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/issues/11632, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.16/9.0.16.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: none of them contains the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App runtime or any WPF or Windows Forms assembly (PresentationCore, PresentationFramework, System.Xaml, System.Windows.Forms and the like), and none contains a native Windows PE file. WPF names appear only as IntelliSense XML documentation files in Microsoft.Private.Intellisense reference packages in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, a Microsoft.Internal.Runtime.WindowsDesktop.Transport package in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts holds runtime libraries such as System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.Diagnostics.EventLog and no WPF or Windows Forms assembly, and WindowsBase.dll appears only as the .NET compatibility facade in the .NET shared framework and its runtime, ILCompiler and reference packs, not the WPF implementation.
